events.title: Claude Opus 5.5 ships
events.detail: Anthropic opens its Claude 5.5 family with an Opus it says performs at the level of Fable 5.1 on most work — at $4 / $20 per Mtok, 20% below Opus 5, with cache reads down 60% to $0.20. 1M-token context by default, 128K max output.

events.title: GPT-6 Sol and Luna reach the API
events.detail: The lower tiers of the GPT-6 family follow Astra into the API: Sol at $2 / $10 and Luna at $0.10 / $0.50 per Mtok for prompts up to 272K tokens. Both are reasoning models with text and image input.

events.title: Grok 4.7 ships
events.detail: xAI — now branded SpaceXAI in its own docs — ships its frontier model for coding, agents and knowledge work at $2 / $6 per Mtok below 200K prompt tokens and $4 / $12 above, with a 500K context window.

events.title: DeepSeek V4.1-Flash cuts the Flash price
events.detail: The smallest model in DeepSeek's new architecture family adds native image understanding and replaces V4 Flash at a lower price: $0.30 / $1.20 per Mtok at peak, half that off-peak. Calls to the old deepseek-v4-flash name are now served by V4.1.

events.title: GPT-6 Astra ships
events.detail: OpenAI releases GPT-6 Astra, 'our most capable model', built to carry complex tasks from the first request to a finished result — at $10 / $50 per Mtok, with prompts over 272K tokens billed at 2x input and 1.5x output.

events.title: Gemini 3.8 Flash goes GA
events.detail: Google's most intelligent Flash yet, aimed at long-horizon software engineering and autonomous agents, ships at $0.75 / $3.75 per Mtok through 2026 — doubling to $1.50 / $7.50 on 2027-01-01.

events.title: Claude Fable 5.1 ships
events.detail: Anthropic's Mythos-class update lands: Terminal-Bench-Science more than doubles to 52.6%, cache reads drop 75% to $0.25 per Mtok, base price holds at $10 / $50. Mythos 5.1 stays gated to vetted US orgs under Project Glasswing.

events.title: Nvidia underwrites 4.25 GW for OpenAI in Ohio
events.detail: Nvidia backs up to $105B of financing for OpenAI's Pike County campus — 4.25 GW in the first phase, 3.75 GW optional, online from 2028. SoftBank's SB Energy builds it and pledges 10 GW of new generation. The single largest compute financing on record.

events.title: Gemini 3.7 Flash goes GA
events.detail: Google's new workhorse Flash for coding and agents lands at an introductory $0.75 / $3.75 per Mtok through 2026, rising to $1.50 / $7.50 on 2027-01-01.

events.title: Grok 4.6 ships
events.detail: xAI's new flagship matches GPT-5.6 Sol on the Artificial Analysis index, one point behind Fable 5, at $2 / $6 per Mtok with a 500K context. Live day one in Cursor, Grok Build and the API. Grok 5 is still in training.

events.title: GPT-5.6 Cyber ships to vetted partners only
events.detail: OpenAI releases a cyber-tuned Sol variant to a trusted tier — Accenture, IBM, CrowdStrike, Cloudflare — through its Daybreak Red program. Frontier capability now ships by clearance level, not by API key.

events.title: Qwen3.8-Max ships
events.detail: Alibaba's 2.4T-parameter MoE (95B active) lands at $2 / $6 per Mtok, with the weights following on Hugging Face ten days later — the first Max-class Qwen ever released openly. Two open '2T+' models from China inside a month.

events.title: OpenAI unveils Astra with ten solved open problems
events.detail: An internal build of OpenAI's next model family closes ten math and TCS problems open for a decade or more — for about $2,000 of inference. Altman demos the multi-agent system to senators and the White House economic team; no release date, and no decision yet on calling it GPT-6.

events.title: Claude Opus 5 ships
events.detail: Anthropic's new Opus, billed as a step-change over Opus 4.8, keeps the $5 / $25 per Mtok price, with a 1M-token context window and 128K max output.

events.title: Google ships three Flash models, still no 3.5 Pro
events.detail: Gemini 3.6 Flash, 3.5 Flash-Lite and 3.5 Flash Cyber land, but the Pro promised at I/O in May stays unshipped after 'internal delays'. Almost as a footnote: DeepMind has started its most ambitious pre-training run yet, for Gemini 4.

events.title: Kimi K3 ships
events.detail: Moonshot's 2.8-trillion-parameter open-weight model lands — the first open '3T-class' model, trailing only Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 on overall capability. China closes the frontier gap.

events.title: GPT-5.6 opens to the public
events.detail: After a two-week federal review, OpenAI clears GPT-5.6 (Sol, Terra, Luna) for everyone — shipped alongside ChatGPT Work, an agent built to carry out whole jobs. The gate lifts.

events.title: Grok 4.5 ships
events.detail: xAI's V9 coding model lands as Grok 4.5 — 1.5T parameters trained on Cursor data, priced at $2 / $6 per Mtok. Still not the fabled 6T Grok 5, which keeps slipping.

events.title: Claude Sonnet 5 ships
events.detail: Anthropic's most agentic Sonnet becomes the default model — near-Opus performance at Sonnet speed and price, aimed squarely at running agents cheaply.

events.title: GPT-5.6 previews under federal gate
events.detail: OpenAI unveils GPT-5.6 — Sol, Terra and Luna — but access is limited to ~20 US-government-vetted partners pending a pre-release review: the frontier's first regulatory chokepoint.

events.title: Claude Fable 5 ships
events.detail: Anthropic opens the Claude 5 family: always-on adaptive thinking and a 1M-token context window.

events.title: GPT-5.5 ships
events.detail: OpenAI's flagship update lands in ChatGPT and Codex; API access follows a day later.

events.title: Claude Opus 4.5 ships
events.detail: Anthropic's strongest coding model to date lands days after Gemini 3 — the frontier cadence compresses to weeks.

events.title: Gemini 3 ships
events.detail: Google's frontier line jumps again; agentic coding and long-horizon tasks improve another step.

events.title: GPT-5.1 ships
events.detail: OpenAI iterates the GPT-5 line with adaptive reasoning effort and faster default paths.

events.title: GPT-5 ships
events.detail: OpenAI unifies reasoning and fast paths behind one router; frontier access goes mass-market.

events.title: Claude 4 ships
events.detail: Anthropic's Opus 4 and Sonnet 4 push sustained autonomous coding into production use.

events.title: Stargate announced: $500B
events.detail: SoftBank, OpenAI, Oracle and MGX commit $500B over four years — $100B deploying immediately — for US AI datacenters.

events.title: DeepSeek-R1 open weights
events.detail: Frontier-class reasoning released under MIT license at a fraction of incumbent training cost.

events.title: OpenAI o1: the reasoning era
events.detail: Test-time compute becomes the new scaling axis — models that think before they answer.

events.title: GPT-4o: omni goes realtime
events.detail: Native audio-vision-text at half the price of GPT-4 Turbo. Frontier intelligence keeps getting cheaper.

events.title: Claude 3 ships
events.detail: Opus matches GPT-4; for the first time the frontier is contested by more than one lab.

events.title: The Techno-Optimist Manifesto
events.detail: Marc Andreessen publishes the manifesto; e/acc ideas enter mainstream venture discourse.

events.title: GPT-4 ships
events.detail: The capability jump that reset every timeline. $30 per million input tokens at launch.

events.title: ChatGPT launches
events.detail: 100M users in two months. The acceleration becomes visible to everyone.

events.title: e/acc is born
events.detail: A pseudonymous newsletter by @zestular, @BasedBeffJezos, @bayeslord and co. names the movement: build, accelerate, ascend the Kardashev gradient.
